evidence: Fixed the wall-clock flake in tests/Playnite.Core.Tests/Serialization/FuzzTargetTests.cs::A_minimum_budget_run_reports_the_completion_marker_and_smaller_budgets_are_rejected without changing product behaviour. The test still runs the target with both budgets at their documented minimums, but it no longer asserts that the iteration budget won the race (the old Budget==iterations and Cases>=MinimumIterations assertions). It now asserts the FUZZ START line reports seconds=30 and iterations=100000, that FUZZ COMPLETE names the same seed, that the completed run did at least one case and that Cases == Clean + Rejected, and it still proves Seconds=29 and Iterations=99999 are rejected by Validate. On the cited run the case itself took 29.272 s of the 30 s wall-clock budget, so the previous assertion was one scheduling hiccup away from failing while the identical run under the new assertions passed. Narrow Release build was warning-free; FuzzTargetTests 18/18 passed locally. linux-ci run 44360090021 on head dd80b2f8b11c6aabc7075484a75f4ffbdeed80c7 succeeded: Playnite.Core.Tests 2287/2287, Playnite.Architecture.Tests 188/188, Playnite.Smoke.Tests 4/4, zero failed and zero skipped, every MTP exit 0. PR https://github.com/seanburkes/playnite-linux/pull/134. No baseline, aggregate or product file changed; no merge by the worker.
